title: The Birthday Wine Mystery
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Inspector Megure, Officer Takagi, forensic tech) omitted by convention -- only the 4 civilian college-friend circle are plot-relevant persons. case_type: attempted_murder (Keiko collapses and is taken away by ambulance; the transcript never confirms a death, so `kills` was not used for the poisoning edge -- `poisons` was used instead). The old lower-fidelity case file (cases/ep328_the_birthday_wine_mystery.json) had the culprit right (Togashi, s2/here p2) but described the density trick as 'gum syrup' -- the transcript actually names it a 'sweetener' packet (like sweetener sinking in iced coffee), so that detail was corrected. The old file also collapsed the glass hand-off into a flat 'was_at' snapshot; the transcript actually specifies an exact chain (Togashi's glass -> Kojima -> Nonaka -> Keiko), which is now direct typed edges. No `event` nodes: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved.

clues.desc: Four fingerprint sets on Keiko's glass (Togashi, Kojima, Nonaka, none matching Keiko) trace the hand-off order and prove the glass was originally Togashi's, not freshly hers.
Chemical analysis: the poison residue in Keiko's glass and the substance in the bottle planted on Nonaka give the exact same reaction -- same poison batch.

Behavioral contrast: everyone who saw Keiko collapse got shaken, but Togashi -- who drank from the same glass moments earlier -- calmly said 'I feel fine,' an oddly confident reaction if he genuinely believed he might be poisoned too.

The planted bottle has no fingerprints on its sides (deliberately wiped) but does have Conan's prints on the bottom from when he'd earlier tucked it back into Togashi's own bag -- proving the bottle started in Togashi's bag and was moved into Nonaka's, not the reverse.

edges.motive_type: jilted_ex_revenge (forced into gift debt, then left for Nonaka)
